questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Recommendations from people that had gone on exchange there before myself.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of stuff to figure out before arriving but in the end I managed to do so.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was some compulsory meetings for exchange students where everyone received important information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing in Isla Vista through the housing facebook groups. There is a lot of housing opportunities there and I would definitely recommend living in Isla Vista.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live in Isla Vista it is where most of the older students live (most freshmen live in the dorms). It is a town with only college students and it is where all the fun stuff happens.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for courses through UCSB Gold. Some classes fill up quickly so be prepared for that. Some classes also required me to go and speak with the professor to ask for permission to join the class after the class had already started.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I talked to some of the other exchange students. If necessary you can also get help from student councilors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes I wanted with the exception of one graduate level course where I did not meet the prerequisites.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be flexible with the courses that you want and have multiple options in case a class is not offered or you are not allowed to enroll in it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both undergraduate and graduate courses. The undergraduate program at UCSB is 4 years so some of their undergraduate courses could also be considered MA level in Denmark.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar. Some courses had both lectures and regular classes, and some had one or the other.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CMPSC 5A - Introduction to Data Science
ECON 181 - International Finance
PSTAT 277B - Advanced Time Series
ECON 170 - Health Economics
ECON 157 - Behavioral Economics
INT 187AM - AI PASTS & FUTURES
ECON 140A - Introduction to Econometrics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend CMPSC 5A and ECON 157 the most. These courses where the most interesting and the ones where i enjoyed learning from them the most.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and housing are very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were so many different activities available. There are multiple sport and athletic opportunities through the university. There is also a wide range of social events available both through and outside of the university. There are also a lot of student clubs at the university that offers activities and excursions that is available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join an intramural team to play sport. I would also recommend to travel a lot while on exchange since there is so many cool places to visit (National parks, LA, SF, Las Vegas, skiing or surfing)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Party in IV or in Downtown Santa Barbara. Go on a lot of trips and explore California.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very Easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Americans are very open and welcoming so be that yourself. I lived and a house with five Americans who were all really friendly and nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are very dependent on their cars.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The college life and vibes at UCSB and in Isla Vista.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have fun, Get to know a bunch of people and go explore a lot of places.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I made and the experiences I had with them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Figuring out all the practical stuff before arriving.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
